extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: Visual Genome is a dataset enabling the modeling of relationships between objects, dense annotations of objects, attributes, and relationships within each image to learn cognitive models. It contains 108,249 images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, bounding boxes, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs, canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO. Dense crowdsourced annotations of region descriptions, objects with bounding boxes, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk over multiple task stages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, User-generated content data, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images taken from the intersection of MS-COCO (328,000 images) and YFCC100M (100 million images), which are real-world, non-iconic images originally uploaded to Flickr by users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were canonicalized to WordNet synsets; region descriptions were enforced to be non-repetitive using BLEU score thresholds (set to 0.7 against image-specific and global descriptions); objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools, lemmatization/stemming, sentence frames, hand-crafted mapping rules, and crowdsourced verification. Stop words were stripped, and descriptions/attributes were lowercased and stripped of excess whitespace for experimental setups.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers created bounding boxes and descriptions (up to 50 region descriptions per image). Objects were extracted from descriptions, mapped with tight bounding boxes, and disambiguated. Attributes and relationships between object pairs were annotated to create region graphs and merged into scene graphs. Workers also created freeform and region-based QA pairs starting with the 'seven Ws'. All annotations were verified using majority voting (3 unique workers) or rapid serial visual presentation judgments.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority voting was performed by three unique workers verifying whether an annotation was factually correct, requiring at least two votes to accept. Rapid serial visual processing-inspired judgments were used to verify objects. For canonicalization, mappings were verified by crowd workers presented with 5 synset choices without revealing the algorithmic proposal.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: On average per image: ~42-50 region descriptions, 21 unique objects, 16-18 attributes, 18-19 relationships, 42 region graphs, 1 scene graph, and 17 question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique crowd workers on AMT. Geographic distribution: 93.02% United States, 1.29% Philippines, 1.13% Kenya, 0.94% India, 0.50% Russia, 0.47% Canada, 2.65% Others. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female. Age: majority between 25 and 34 years old (range: 18 to 68 years old). Workers were paid $6-$8 per hour.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP / dependency parser, WordNet lexeme counts, word2vec, BLEU score computation
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people (people-related categories like man, person, woman are the most frequent) and sports (e.g. ski, ballplayer, racket, skiing, surfboarding) due to the underlying source images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings still contain some ambiguity. Discriminative models struggle with predicting relationships due to high intra-class appearance variability. Baseline visual question answering models struggle with long-tail distributions and complex reasoning ('where' and 'why' questions).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Cognitive computer vision and NLP tasks: dense image captioning, visual question answering, image understanding and evaluation, visual relationship extraction, action recognition, semantic image retrieval, and object/attribute detection.
